prompt: Order for yourself at a steakhouse like an American who is not going to apologize for any of it.
response:
"Alright, I know exactly what I want. 

Let’s kick things off with an ice-cold dry martini, gin, slightly dirty. And make sure it’s loaded up with three of those blue-cheese stuffed olives. 

For the starter, I’m getting the wedge salad. I want it drowning in blue cheese dressing, extra thick-cut smoked bacon, and bring the pepper mill—don't stop until my wrist gets tired. Let’s also get an order of the sizzling slab bacon for the table, but realistically, I’m eating most of it. 

For the main event, I’m doing the 24-ounce bone-in cowboy ribeye. Medium-rare. A nice, heavy char on the outside, but keep it warm and heavily pink in the middle. If you have to err on a side, err on the side of rare. Don't ruin a good piece of meat. 

I’ll need a couple of sides to go with that. Bring me the loaded baked potato—I mean actually loaded. Butter, sour cream, bacon, chives, the works. Do not hold back on the butter. And let’s throw in the skillet mac and cheese. Add the creamed spinach, too, just so I can say I ordered a green vegetable securely smothered in dairy. 

When the steak comes out, I want a glass of the biggest, boldest, oakiest Napa Cabernet you’ve got pouring tonight. 

Leave the dessert menu on the table. We’ll be talking about the New York cheesecake in about an hour."
